text:
lee: Noticed tenant-88 is 'ping-ponging' routes again when cost and latency scores are almost identical. Happens even w/ affinity set.

anika: saw that on friday. looks like our selector re-evaluates per-retry with no memory -> flips.

jorge: is this on hedged hedged or single?

lee: single-shot. attaching short excerpt from logs (cleaned):
```
select: cand-us score 0.6014
select: cand-eu score 0.6013
selected: cand-eu
metric: backend_tmp_penalty[cand-eu]=0.004
next: cand-us score 0.6015
selected: cand-us
```

maya: this is deterministic noise from penalty jitter + our tiny score resolution (4 decimal). two quick ideas: bump score precision to 6 decimals OR add a stability window where we prefer previous selection if delta < epsilon.

anika: prefer stability window. raising precision may hide real small deltas and makes rollouts harder. also fewer flips in dashboards.

lee: agree. what about tenants that want aggressive cost savings? they might prefer re-eval every request.

jorge: add a tenant-level opt-in: policy.stability.prefer_previous: true/false. default true.

maya: and a global stability_window_ms with per-tenant override. default 1000ms. Also track route_last_selected_at in the scoring cache so the window is enforced.

lee: careful: scoring cache is currently LRU with small TTL. If we increase retention we might bias selection towards cold pods. Need warmup_hint integration.

anika: propose hybrid approach: stability applies only if candidate has recent successful request within warmup_threshold_ms (say 30s) OR warmup_hint=false. otherwise allow re-eval. That avoids sticking to cold GPUs.

jorge: I can prototype selector changes. rough pseudo: 
```
if score_delta < epsilon and now - last_selected < stability_window and candidate.warm?:
  choose previous
else:
  normal select
```

sara: please log tie_break_mode and chosen_reason for every select. that'll help prove improvement in sim.

ops-bot: canary deployment scheduled: routing-decider v0.9.7 -> canary (pending)

anika: metrics to add: route_spin_rate (per-tenant), stability_hit_rate, warmup_rejects, and selected_reason tag. alert if route_spin_rate > 0.3% over 10m for top-50 tenants.

maya: also add a histogram of score_deltas at decision time. we'll see epsilon distribution.

lee: one more complexity: region_affinity is higher priority for Dedicated. Rollout must respect tenant_tiers. Add precedence: tenant_override > dedicated_defaults > global. document in RFC.

jorge: on warmup_hint, we should add estimated_warmup_cost_tokens for GPU-backed candidates so the selector can penalize cold starts when cost delta small. e.g., effective_cost = measured_cost + warmup_estimate * weight.

anika: love that. small caveat: warmup_estimate must be model/hardware specific. keep default conservative.

ops-bot: canary started: routing-decider v0.9.7 -> 2/2 canaries healthy

sara: running a 12h sim across traffic mixes now (interactive/batch/preview). will upload results. if route_spin_rate drops while overall latency & cost stable -> we ship.

lee: sgtm. followups: 1) impl selector with stability window + warmup check, 2) add metrics/alerts, 3) tenant opt-in flags and precedence doc, 4) sim + canary. i'll write a short RFC summarizing tradeoffs.

anika: thanks. tagging @eng-sre for alert thresholds.

ops-bot: canary finished: routing-decider v0.9.7 -> 2/2 canaries healthy for 30m

sara: sim update: route_spin_rate down ~82% for interactive workloads, negligible cost diff, a few warmup rejections flagged for tiny tenants. posting full numbers in RI-9047.

lee: nice. let's roll to staging and keep close watch.

maya: i'll draft the RFC and include microbenchmarks for warmup_estimate values.

lee: closing thread, will link RFC and sim artifacts in RI-9047. :white_check_mark:
